title: Custom aim and resolver logic must steer native ragebot via plist yaw offsets
author: agy-extract
body:
- Executor environment lacks synthetic input APIs (no mouse1click, mousemoverel, or keypress), and VirtualInputManager events are rejected by the client.
- Camera writes are overwritten every frame (60 Hz) by the game engine's camera controller, preventing direct camera-driven aim control.
- The cheat Lua API provides no aim-point setter (e.g. rage.override_aim_point) or manual shot trigger (e.g. rage.force_fire).
- Custom resolvers must operate strictly as guidance layers by feeding yaw adjustments into the native ragebot via plist.set ("Force body yaw" and "Override yaw offset"), delegating raycasting, hitchance checks, backtrack, and fire dispatch to the native engine.

title: Dual authentication in feed receiver supporting license sessions and master token fallback
author: agy-extract
body:
- Endpoints (/ingest, /config, /script.lua, /version) accept authentication via either X-Token (master owner token) or X-Session (license key session).
- Events sent with X-Session are tagged lic=<key name>; events sent with X-Token are tagged owner.
- Client st.auth() prioritizes the active loader session and only falls back to the manual token input when unauthenticated.
- License users have streaming locked on by default; only verified master token holders can toggle event streaming off.

title: Live feed receiver on pve2 LXC routed through WireGuard VPS reverse proxy
author: agy-extract
body:
- Ingest service runs inside an unprivileged LXC (VMID 115, `10.8.0.8`) on pve2, binding only to the WireGuard tunnel address.
- Inbound connections route from public VPS Caddy (`feed.sites.exxo.world`) across the WireGuard tunnel; no local router ports are opened.
- Caddy strictly whitelists exposed paths (`/ingest`, `/health`, `/config`, `/script.lua`, `/auth`), returning 404 for all others.
- WireGuard peers on the VPS can be added live via `wg set` without restarting the tunnel or interrupting existing peers.

title: Script release channels: stable / beta with numbered builds
author: agy-extract
body:
- Every deployment creates a sequential build number (#1, #2, ...) stored on the server so builds can be promoted or rolled back without rebuilding.
- Accounts on the beta list receive the beta build; everyone else receives stable.
- Clients detect updates within a minute and download the channel's build on loader reload.
- Deploy to beta via `scripts/deploy.sh --beta --note "..."` and promote tested builds to stable via `scripts/hvh release promote`.
- Rolling stable back also rolls back beta when beta is tracking stable (`scripts/hvh release rollback stable <id>`).

title: Admin session persistence across service restarts via hashed admin_sessions.json
author: agy-extract
body:
- What: Admin sessions are persisted to `admin_sessions.json` alongside `admin.json` (chmod 0600) and restored on service startup.
- Why: In-memory session storage caused admins to be logged out on every code deployment or service restart.
- Security: Stores only hashed session tokens (preventing token theft if the file is copied) and binds sessions to current credentials so running `hvhctl admin setup` invalidates active sessions.
- Expiration: Preserves 30-minute idle timeout and 12-hour max session lifespan across restarts (idle clock drift up to ~1 min).

title: Darklua local-only renaming for client script obfuscation and minification
author: agy-extract
body:
- Rejected full Lua VM obfuscation (Prometheus Vmify): output bloated to 29 MB, preventing in-game download and compilation.
- Dual VM protection rejected: ineffective against attackers controlling the client VM who hook `loadstring` or `http.get` to dump decrypted plaintext during execution.
- Script protection relies on lightweight Darklua renaming + per-key watermarking (`UNSYK_LICENSE`) and moving core logic server-side, rather than client-side VM walls.

title: Keyless guest session architecture for stable release channel
author: agy-extract
body:
- Unkeyed loader fallback: When no license key is present, the loader requests a guest session via /auth passing local Roblox username and UserId.
- Namespace isolation: Guest sessions are logged as guest:<RobloxName> across sessions, telemetry, and journal logs to avoid colliding with licensed users.
- Channel isolation: Guests are strictly pinned to the stable channel even if their username appears on the beta list; beta channel requires a valid key.
- Abuse guards: Rate-limited to 30 logins per IP per 10 minutes; cloud config saving is rejected for guests to prevent disk exhaustion.
- Killswitch: Set GUEST_ACCESS=0 in /etc/hvh-ingest.env to disable guest access and return server to keys-only mode.

title: Prometheus rename-only obfuscation replacing darklua and ban on string encryption
author: agy-extract
body:
- Replaced Darklua with Prometheus for client script obfuscation (57% source size reduction).
- String encryption is strictly prohibited: in Lua, table field accesses (e.g. st.x, obj.Text) are string lookups, so string encryption converts every access into a function call and table lookup, dropping framerate from ~120 fps to ~10 fps across paint and tick callbacks.
- scripts/prometheus.config.lua must keep steps empty (local variable renaming and comment stripping only); scripts/obfuscate.sh enforces a build check failing if string encryption is enabled.

title: Prometheus string-encryption obfuscation replacing Darklua without VM presets
author: agy-extract
body:
- Replaced Darklua with Prometheus (levno-710) CLI executed locally via LuaJIT; eliminates dependency on browser-based Luvyn Studio wrapper (which runs client-side in a WASM worker with no backend API).
- Configured with EncryptStrings + ConstantArray + local renaming; produces ~500KB ASCII-clean output in ~1s and preserves API globals (entity, rage, aa, UNSYK_*) intact while encrypting string literals and menu labels.
- Rejected Prometheus VM presets (Full Medium/Strong with Vmify, control-flow flattening, NumbersToExpressions): expanded 311KB source script to 29MB (9364% increase, 3-minute build time), which exceeds in-game HTTP download and loadstring limits and risks custom sandbox compatibility.

title: Rolling HMAC heartbeat token echo and deferred soft-degrade for client DRM
author: agy-extract
body:
- Lua VM is attacker-controlled; static stops or local checks are easily hooked or stubbed with fake 200 responses.
- Server /beat issues a rolling per-account HMAC token (5-min window, keyed off INGEST_TOKEN); client (unsyk.lua) must capture and echo it in feed batches (/ingest).
- Server validates token echo and stamps beat_ok per event, surfacing spoofed heartbeats in hvhctl abuse without relying on client honesty.
- Client soft-degrade (lic_enf remote config key): instead of hard-stopping, resolver detunes yaw error after 240s without authenticated beat, keeping legitimate users (who auth <60s) unaffected while degrading pirated copies.

title: Server-side resolver candidate generation with per-build HMAC seed scrambling
author: agy-extract
body:
- Moved candidate offsets, priors, and scoring weights from hardcoded client tables (`st.rsx`) to server-side generator `server/hvh_resolver.py` exposed via `server/receiver.py`.
- Generates candidate slots and signs per build using an HMAC of `SESSION_SECRET` + `UNSYK_BUILD` (`UNSYK_RSEED`), invalidating static memory dumps across builds (~96% mismatch across consecutive builds).
- Versioned via `rv` (incremented via `GEN` in `hvh_resolver.py`); client script checks `rv` during heartbeat (`/beat` or `/me`), refetches on version changes, and purges table on revoked sessions.
- Employs `/me?resolver=1` query fallback to avoid 404s from VPS Caddy reverse proxy blocking unwhitelisted `/resolver` and `/beat` paths.

title: Two-tier remote config with per-account overrides and unified versioning
author: agy-extract
body:
- Two-tier remote config incorporates a client-to-server telemetry loop so the admin panel reflects real in-game state rather than static mid-range defaults.
- Client script (unsyk.lua) checks 58 controllable settings every 5s and dispatches a `settings` event on change (and at least 1/min), transmitting both active values and pre-override baselines.
- Server (server/receiver.py) aggregates reported settings into `live_vals` per account within status responses.
- Admin panel (server/admin/app.js) seeds inputs with live values, shows sync status pills (green for synced, amber for pending poll or remote control disabled), and highlights "mixed" states across accounts.

title: Abuse tamper detection flags older clients as tampered unless gated by build number
author: agy-extract
body:
- Verifying heartbeat token echoes in server ingest marks batches from older client builds as beat_ok=False because older versions do not echo the token.
- Marking no-beat=100% as TAMPERED directly results in false positives across all active subscribers until they restart and update to an echo-capable build.
- Always condition TAMPERED flags on whether the reported client build supports the token echo, reporting older builds as unverified (no-beat=old) instead of tampered.

title: AIM WAIT telemetry misinterprets target snapshot memory and bolt cycling as hold hesitation
author: agy-extract
body:
- The cheat client retains target snapshots in memory for 15–19 ticks after line of sight is broken or a shot is fired.
- Raw 'no-shot' episodes falsely appear as aim hesitation: many are leftover target data from an immediate prior shot (<0.1s post-fire), weapon bolt cycling delays (Scout/AWP), or fleeting glimpses lasting only 1–2 ragebot scans.
- Telemetry analysis must categorize AIM WAIT episodes into leftovers, bolt cycling, glimpses, and real holds to isolate true aim hesitation.

title: Anchored character rigs lack Humanoid velocity breaking custom stop and movement prediction
author: agy-extract
body:
- Local and enemy character rigs are anchored parts moved directly by the game engine rather than unanchored physics Humanoids.
- movement.get_velocity returns (0, 0, 0) for both local and enemy characters, causing custom velocity-based auto-stop methods to fail.
- movement.predict_position produces zero extrapolation across all tick horizons (4, 8, and 16 ticks), yielding error identical to assuming the target stays static.
- Peek and teleport prediction requires deriving velocity independently from tick-by-tick position history.

title: Cheat loader blocks scripts referencing engine classes like RemoteEvent
author: agy-extract
body:
- The cheat loader performs static validation on downloaded scripts before execution and aborts with "lua violation: blocked class '<ClassName>'".
- Blocks classes like RemoteEvent (and potentially VirtualInputManager), even though luac -p passes syntax checks cleanly.
- Avoid referencing restricted engine class names in diagnostic scans, probes, or reflection helpers.

title: Cheat Lua API cannot toggle auto stop or resolve internal menu references
author: agy-extract
body:
- Host cheat Lua API provides no function to toggle or control auto stop, and cannot drive player movement.
- `ui.reference` fails to resolve internal menu elements (196 probed candidate names for Auto Stop and Double Tap returned no matches); internal auto stop must be manually disabled by the user in the cheat GUI.
- Menu toggle readouts (e.g. Double Tap charge) cannot be read via menu references, even though native double tap fires properly.

title: Cheat Lua API double-tap charge read always reports 0 blocking defensive tick shifts
author: agy-extract
body:
- `dt_state().charged` (or host double-tap charge read) always reports 0/uncharged in the cheat Lua runtime.
- Gating defensive bursts on the charged state prevents `rage.force_shift` from ever firing.
- Workaround: Fire `rage.force_shift` unconditionally whenever the shift tick setting is greater than 0.

title: Combat hit and miss events always report id 0 and require target matching
author: agy-extract
body:
- In-game hit and miss callback events always report `id = 0` instead of referencing the originating shot ID.
- Correlating which shot caused a hit or miss requires matching against the target player name and shot timestamp.
- The double-tap (DT) API charge readout persistently reports `0/14` even when double tap is active and firing two shots per tick; the API charge value cannot be relied on.

title: debug.info is blocked in cheat Lua sandbox, requiring callback profiling by registration order
author: agy-extract
body:
- The cheat's Lua runtime blocks debug.info, preventing dynamic reflection of source lines or function names during runtime profiling.
- Callback profilers must track and identify callbacks by registration order or explicit labels rather than inspecting the call stack.

title: deploy.sh --beta deploys server components live to production for all users
author: agy-extract
body:
- `deploy.sh --beta` only isolates client Lua script releases to the beta channel.
- Server components (feed receiver, hvhctl, admin panel) are deployed live to production for all users during a beta deploy.
- Any uncommitted or in-progress server edits in the local workspace will immediately go live to production when deploying beta.

title: Double tap disables fake lag and forces packet choke count to zero
author: agy-extract
body:
- Enabling Double Tap (DT) in the cheat engine disables fake lag, causing `get_choked_ticks` to continuously return 0.
- Features relying on packet choking (e.g., tick-synchronized flick desync or unchoke mechanics) will fail to trigger while DT is enabled.
- The cheat Lua API cannot toggle DT programmatically because menu item references cannot be resolved; DT must be toggled off manually in the cheat menu.

title: Game characters lack Humanoids and use anchored parts, preventing custom physics quick-stop
author: agy-extract
body:
- Target game characters lack a Humanoid instance; player models consist of anchored parts positioned directly by the game's custom movement script.
- Lua quick-stop implementations relying on Roblox physics, velocity damping, or Humanoid state manipulation cannot decelerate or stop the player.
- Prior self-tests that appeared to validate custom quick-stop were false positives caused by the cheat client's native auto-stop engaging.
- Quick-stop controls were hidden from the menu and stripped from presets as a result.

title: get_anim_state desync returns a constant 84 and cannot be used for resolver or desync tracking
author: agy-extract
body:
- get_anim_state(player).desync returns a constant 84 for nearly all players rather than a live desync angle.
- Cannot be used to determine real feet yaw, LBY, or true desync side; do not rely on it for resolver or anti-aim logic.

title: luac -p syntax check does not validate Luau or host runtime compatibility
author: agy-extract
body:
- Standard `luac -p` only tests against Lua 5.x grammar and cannot validate Luau syntax, type annotations, or host environment globals.
- Files that pass local `luac -p` syntax checks can still fail to parse or execute in the in-game Luau runtime.
- The loader incorporates local compile/run try-catches with fallback to the last working cached copy and on-screen diagnostics.

title: Luau 200-local limit in desync_aa.lua requires storing state on st table
author: agy-extract
body:
- Lua 5.1 and Luau enforce a hard limit of 200 local variables per function or chunk scope.
- desync_aa.lua has reached this limit at the script/chunk level; adding new top-level local declarations causes compiler errors.
- Store any new persistent variables or feature flags as fields on the existing state table (st.<property>) instead of declaring new locals.

title: Plain deploy.sh publishes working tree as stable build
author: agy-extract
body:
- Running deploy.sh with no flags publishes the current working tree directly as the stable build.
- If the working tree contains unfinished beta features or profiler experiments, a plain deploy will accidentally leak them to stable users.
- Use deploy.sh --beta --raw to update server and loader infrastructure while leaving stable untouched.

title: Prometheus WrapInFunction triggers Lua 200-local limit on chunks near ceiling
author: agy-extract
body:
- Prometheus wraps target scripts in an outer function (WrapInFunction) to hoist constant arrays and string-decoding routines into the chunk.
- If the script's main chunk is already near Lua's 200-local ceiling, WrapInFunction pushes the chunk over the limit, causing parse errors (too many local variables).
- Fix: Wrap self-contained top-level blocks (e.g. debug logger, inactive Discord integration) in IIFEs (;(function() ... end)()) to reduce top-level locals and provide headroom before running Prometheus.

title: Reported shot hitchance is unreliable and inaccuracy cannot auto-detect no-spread
author: agy-extract
body:
- Shot event callbacks report hitchance as 0 approximately 50% of the time even for valid scoped shots; log the script's intended hitchance/min damage alongside reported values to verify overrides.
- Cheat calculates and reports identical `inaccuracy` values on both spread and no-spread servers; no-spread environment cannot be auto-detected via inaccuracy metrics and requires a manual switch or server profile.

title: Roblox top-bar offset auto-calibration fails when clicks hit adjacent controls
author: agy-extract
body:
- Heuristic Roblox top-bar offset calculation (~36 px) fails across varying resolutions/window modes, causing click coordinates to land one row low.
- Offset auto-calibration that only re-learns on clicks missing all controls silently fails when the shift lands on an adjacent control (registered as a valid hit).
- Solved by showing a one-time center-crosshair click calibration on first window open (persisted permanently) with a manual recalibration fallback in the UI.

title: State files written by root hvhctl must be chowned to the dynamic service user
author: agy-extract
body:
- When admin CLI tools (`hvhctl`) run as root and rewrite state files (`keys.json`) consumed by a systemd `DynamicUser=` service, the file becomes root-owned with 0600 permissions and unreadable by the service.
- Unreadable state files must raise fatal errors instead of defaulting to an empty collection; treating unreadable files as empty causes subsequent saves (e.g., via the admin panel) to overwrite and wipe all existing keys.
- State-saving routines running as root must explicitly restore ownership to the dynamic service user and keep a previous backup (`keys.json.bak`).
- State read failures in the auth receiver must return HTTP 503 ("try again later") rather than HTTP 401 ("unknown key") to prevent client scripts from self-terminating.

title: The user's game account is license tigokraft, not owner
author: agy-extract
body:
- The user's in-game account/license identifier is `tigokraft`, not `owner`.
- `owner` represents only the master token used for administrative operations.
- Enrolling the user in beta or running account tests requires using `tigokraft` (e.g., `scripts/hvh beta add tigokraft`, `--lic tigokraft`, `--acct tigokraft`).

title: VPS Caddy reverse proxy 404s new endpoints unless explicitly allowlisted in Caddyfile
author: agy-extract
body:
- New backend endpoints (such as `/auth`) return 404 externally until explicitly added to the reverse proxy matcher in the VPS `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`.
- Caddy does not route wildcard paths to the receiver by default; only explicitly configured route blocks are proxied through WireGuard to the backend LXC.

title: High per-call cheat API overhead requires per-tick memoization and throttled updates
author: agy-extract
body:
- Host cheat API calls (reading entity info, plist.set) have high overhead (50–100 µs per call); uncoordinated reads across separate callbacks (resolver, intel, teleport detector) consumed >500 ms/s of Lua time, causing in-game fps to drop to ~40.
- Read each enemy's entity data once per tick into a shared memoized table reused across all callbacks (intel, resolver, detector, feed).
- Throttle slow-changing queries: cache enemy names per entity lifecycle, poll weapon names every 16 ticks, and read ping once per tick.
- Push state mutations (e.g. plist.set overrides) only on change, using a safety refresh every 32 ticks instead of writing every tick.
